subject: great bustard
title: Great Bustard Males Eat a Poison That Kills Most Animals

scenes.text: Before mating season, these males eat something that kills most animals.
Every spring, male great bustards go looking for blister beetles.
The beetles carry cantharidin, a poison that can kill people in small doses.
In Spain, beetles turned up in 43 percent of male droppings, about twice the rate in females.
Why? The same poison fights gut bacteria and worms.
A healthier male may look better to females. So the poison could be part of the show.

description:
Male great bustards eat toxic blister beetles in spring, the mating season, about twice as often as females: beetles turned up in 43 percent of male droppings versus 20 percent of female droppings.
The beetles contain cantharidin, which is lethal to most animals in small doses but also kills bacteria and gut parasites. Researchers think a parasite-free male may look fitter to females.
Would you eat poison to impress someone?
thumbnail_text: HE EATS POISON TO IMPRESS HER
first_comment: Females eat the beetles too, just half as often. Medicine, showing off, or both?
